_why_distinguished_by_repeats_the_member: ART-167. Two of the owner's archives carry the top-level directory
the same BoingBag's contributed extras. Measured (44 archives walked,
and `XAD-Update`; the Contribution archive's holds `Contribution` and

2. This package's `Install` script, line 1615, runs
`C/Updater AmigaOS-Update "<target>"` — identical in shape to
One thing 3.9-1 has no counterpart for: line 1632 runs the Updater a

_why_post_install: ART-227, and this one is the whole reason the mechanism exists.
BoingBag 2's `Updater` writes its ROM update as
`Devs/AmigaOS ROM Update.BB39-2` — **321 768 bytes** — and leaves it there,
beside the CD's own 127 956-byte `Devs/AmigaOS ROM Update`, under a name
`SetPatch` does not load. Measured on 2026-08-24 on the tree ART's own run
produced: both files present, the old one still the active one. So a tree that
reports itself BoingBag'd, and answers `Workbench 45.3` when asked, is running
the ROM update it had before. Nothing fails; the newer file is simply never
HstWB Installer does the same move — back the old one aside, copy the new one
over it — which is where this was found. ART does it on the host instead of in
the boot script, for the reasons `core::amigainstall::finish` gives.
**`NSDPatch.cfg` is deliberately left alone.** BoingBag 1 leaves
(the two packages do not even agree on the punctuation), and neither is rotated
here. That file is user-editable configuration; a reference copy beside it is
the right shape, and HstWB reaches the same conclusion by touching neither.
_why_follow_ups: ART-280, and it was measured before it was declared. On a chain ART
itself produced (clean AmigaOS 3.9 tree -> BoingBag 1 -> BoingBag 2,
every file of every state hashed, 2026-09-08) `Libs/xadmaster.library`
reads `xadmaster 9.0 (25.11.2000)` clean, `9.1 (05.01.2001)` after
BoingBag 1 - whose payload carries that 105 368-byte build - and
**9.1 still** after BoingBag 2. So this package's second payload was
never applied, and 9.1 is below the 10 the gate names.
What it applies: `BoingBag3.9-2/XAD-Update` is a second ZipCrypto
archive inside the same wrapper, 152 837 bytes, 39 entries, every one
encrypted - `Libs/xadmaster.library` at 110 100 bytes, 26 `Libs/xad/*`
clients and 10 `C/` tools. Nothing here decrypts it: the package's own
`Updater` does, on the Amiga, exactly as it does for `AmigaOS-Update`
(ART-166, and the owner's recorded ruling that ART writes no bypass).
The shape is HstWB Installer's, read from its own source rather than
reasoned about - the one distribution builder whose scripts can be
read (MIT), `amiga/amiga-os-3.9/S/Amiga-OS-3.9/Install-Boing-Bag-2`
lines 32-36:
; run xad updater, if xadmaster.library version is less than 10
Version >>SYS:hstwb-installer.log "SYS:Libs/xadmaster.library" 10 FILE
IF WARN
SYS:T/BoingBags/BoingBag3.9-2/C/Updater SYS:T/BoingBags/BoingBag3.9-2/XAD-Update "SYS:"
ENDIF
Two things this is NOT, both of which an earlier round got wrong and
which are corrected here rather than left standing (2026-09-08):
1. NOT a second emulator run. HstWB does it in the same boot, four
lines after the first invocation, and so does ART - it is more
lines in the one script `workvol::startup_sequence` already
writes, not another ~140 s cycle.
2. NOT behind a requester. The `#install-xad-update` requester lives
in this package's own `Install` script, and ART does not run that
script: it runs `C/Updater` directly. Nobody is asked anything by
the program ART actually launches.
`program` and `args` are relative to this package's drawer, exactly
like `amiga_installer.program` above; the target volume is appended by
the composer because it is a fact about the run. The gate's `path` is
relative to the **system** volume, and the script prefixes it.
One trap, recorded because it is the reason this is a designed change
and not a one-line append: `Version ... FILE` signals `older than
that` by SETTING WARN - it is the answer, not an error - so a gate
emitted above the script's own `If Warn` would overwrite the
installer's verdict with the gate's, and every successful run on a
tree with an old `xadmaster` would be reported as `the installer said
no`. The follow-up block is emitted strictly below the result capture.

_why_extra_members: ART-280, from the host. `amiga_installer.follow_ups` above is the same fact for the
emulator route - a second `C/Updater` invocation - and this is the host route's: the same
second payload, the same gate, placed by ART instead of by the package's own program.
Both are declared because both routes exist and neither is the other's fallback.
**What it carries, measured** (the owner's own `BoingBag39-2.lha`, member `XAD-Update`,
every entry decrypted with the key above and listed, 2026-09-08): 39 entries, 152 837
bytes, top level exactly `C` and `Libs` - 9 `C/` tools, 26 `Libs/xad/*` clients and
`Libs/xadmaster.library` at 110 100 bytes. So two subtree rules cover it whole, and no
rule here names a path the archive does not have.
**The gate is HstWB Installer's, read from its own source** (MIT,
`amiga/amiga-os-3.9/S/Amiga-OS-3.9/Install-Boing-Bag-2`, lines 32-36): `Version
"SYS:Libs/xadmaster.library" 10 FILE` / `IF WARN` / run the updater on `XAD-Update`. The
number is 10 because that is what those lines say, not because anything here chose it.
**Why the gate can be read before the main member is placed.** `AmigaOS-Update` carries
121 files and **no `Libs/xadmaster.library`** among them - which is also why the round-3
measurement found the library still at 9.1 after a real BoingBag 2 run - so the tree's
answer is the same before and after. Reading it first is what lets every file this unit
would overwrite be checked against `distribution.json` before a byte is written.
**How the version is read on the host, and the reading that had to be corrected.** This
file carries **no `$VER:` marker at all** - searched byte by byte on 2026-09-08 across the
owner's 9.0 (105 332 bytes, off the CD), 9.1 (105 368, BoingBag 1) and 10.0 (110 100,
`XAD-Update`) copies, zero hits in each. What each carries at offset ~384 is its `struct
Resident`: `xadmaster.library\0` followed by `xadmaster 9.0 (25.11.2000)`. So
`core::amigaver::read_id_string` reads that, anchored on the file's own name, and a
`$VER:`-only reader would have answered *nothing* for the one file this gate is about.
_why_post_place: The host-side counterpart of `amiga_installer.post_install` above, and it is deliberately
**not the same list** - the two routes leave different work behind, so one shared list
would have to be wrong on one of them.
1. `Devs/AmigaOS ROM Update` - identical to the Amiga-side step, and needed for the same
reason (ART-227): the payload writes its 321 768-byte ROM update as
`Devs/AmigaOS ROM Update.BB39-2`, beside the CD's own 127 956-byte file, under a name
`SetPatch` does not load. Whoever puts the payload down - the Updater or ART - leaves
the same two files, so the same rotation is owed.
2. `Devs/NSDPatch.cfg` - **only on this route**, and this reverses what the
`_why_post_install` note above still records for the other one. That note's reasoning
(the file is user-editable configuration; HstWB touches neither) is kept there because
it is still what the Amiga-side route does. Emu68 Hatcher, which is the project ART's
host placement follows, renames it into place -
`("Devs/NSDPatch.cfg.BB39-2", "Devs", "NSDPatch.cfg")` in its `boingbag.py` - and the
owner's 2026-09-08 decision is to do what that project does. The user's own file is not
lost: `replace-keeping-backup` moves it to `Devs/NSDPatch.cfg.old` first, and refuses
rather than overwriting once four generations exist.
Recorded as a **known divergence from the Updater's own tree**: the real Updater leaves
`NSDPatch.cfg` alone, so a host placement checked against the run-8 snapshot differs on
exactly these two paths (`Devs/NSDPatch.cfg` changed, `Devs/NSDPatch.cfg.old` added),
for this reason and no other.
**`rename-into-place` was asked for and `replace-keeping-backup` is what shipped.** The
brief's own words were "keeping a backup the same way", which is this step exactly; a
second variant differing only in whether the source file is left behind would be one more
thing for a reader to tell apart, and leaving `Devs/NSDPatch.cfg.BB39-2` in place is also
what the Updater's own tree does.
_why_chain_position: 3 of the material's own order. BoingBag 3.9-2's own Install script reads version.library off the target and requires revision >= 2, which is BoingBag 3.9-1 applied - the arrow between rows 2 and 3, enforced by the package rather than advised by prose.
_why_overrides: records at length: `overrides` is a claim about which **component the tree's manifest says
placed a file**, and AmigaOS 3.9's recipe splits the Workbench between `workbench-base` and
`workbench-39`. Counted against the owner's own tree: of this payload's 121 files, 84 are
recorded to `workbench-39`, 17 to `workbench-base` and 20 are new. The `XAD-Update` unit
below lands on 29 more `workbench-39` files and 7 new ones, and is covered by the same
list - its items are this package's, under this package's component id.
`boingbag-39-1` is here because BoingBag 1 rewrites many of the same paths first, and once
it has, the manifest records **it** as the owner - so without this line the second BoingBag
would be refused on exactly the trees the chain is designed to produce.
